reading.body:
This facility is a cable landing station on the Jersey Shore where Tata Communications, a global telecommunications operator, terminates international subsea cables. Cable landing stations are network infrastructure rather than data centers, designed to receive and route data from submarine cables rather than to host compute. No published IT power capacity figures exist for this site, consistent with its function as a cable termination point.

Within New Jersey's mapped data center geography, this facility does not appear in the five sites that publish megawatt figures. The state has 48 mapped facilities total and 111.3 MW of published IT capacity across them. The ranking assigned here reflects a data structure issue rather than operational scale: no power specification was found to rank.

For a reader assessing AI infrastructure, this site matters as network backbone rather than as a location for AI workloads. International cable landings are foundational to moving data at scale, but they do not directly constrain or enable accelerator deployment. Whether Tata Communications or other operators use this landing to feed nearby colocation or hyperscaler facilities would depend on facts not published here.
